name: United Kingdom (UK-wide layer)
legalSystem: common law (England and Wales, Northern Ireland); mixed (Scotland)
note: Death registration is devolved (England and Wales, Scotland, Northern Ireland each have their own registrar general and statute); this layer records what happens after registration at UK level. Registrars and the Registrars General in Great Britain must send death particulars to the Department for Work and Pensions, and the DWP-run Tell Us Once service, offered by the registrar, lets one informant notify HMRC, HM Passport Office, DVLA, the local council (including electoral registration) and several public pension schemes in one go. Tell Us Once is not available for people living in Northern Ireland. There is no UK population register and no official death-data service for banks, insurers or other private bodies: the family contacts them, normally with a certificate. A general information gateway to registered digital verification services exists in the Data (Use and Access) Act 2025 but is not yet in force.

steps.title: Local registrar sends death particulars to DWP
steps.who: Each registrar of births and deaths in England and Wales employed by a local authority that facilitates the notification service (Tell Us Once), for deaths they register or declarations they attest; not where the registration follows a coroner's certificate after an inquest.
steps.trigger: Registration of the death (or attestation of a declaration made to another registrar).

deadline.text: as soon as reasonably practicable after the death is registered

steps.latencyNote: as soon as reasonably practicable after the death is registered (ssnd-2012-r5)
steps.summary: Regulations under s. 125 of the Social Security Administration Act 1992 put a duty on registrars to furnish DWP with the death particulars, in writing, which may be electronic. This is the base feed that stops benefits and pensions without the family acting.

steps.title: Registrars General (England and Wales; Scotland) send death particulars to DWP
steps.who: The Registrar General for England and Wales (for all deaths registered there) and the Registrar General for Scotland (for deaths notified to them).

deadline.text: within such period as the Secretary of State may specify, or as soon as reasonably practicable where the local authority facilitates the notification service

steps.latencyNote: as soon as reasonably practicable where the notification service is facilitated; otherwise within a period the Secretary of State specifies (ssnd-2012-r5)
steps.summary: The central registers in Great Britain also feed DWP, so every registered death in England, Wales and Scotland reaches the benefits system whether or not the family uses Tell Us Once.

steps.title: Informant uses Tell Us Once
steps.who: The person registering the death (or anyone given the unique reference number by the registrar), with permission from the spouse or civil partner, next of kin, executor or administrator. Available where the deceased lived in England, Scotland or Wales.
steps.trigger: Registration of the death, or a coroner's interim death certificate where an inquest is under way.

deadline.text: within 28 days of getting the unique reference number

steps.summary: The registrar either completes Tell Us Once with the informant or gives them a reference number to use online or by phone. The service is run for DWP under the 'notification service' defined in the 2012 Regulations and passes the death to the bodies below.

steps.title: Tell Us Once notifies HMRC
steps.who: Tell Us Once (DWP) to HM Revenue and Customs.
steps.summary: HMRC is told so it can deal with personal tax and cancel benefits and credits such as Child Benefit.

steps.title: Tell Us Once cancels DWP benefits and State Pension
steps.who: Tell Us Once to the DWP benefit and pension systems.
steps.summary: DWP cancels benefits and entitlements such as Universal Credit or State Pension and contacts the family about any over- or under-payment.

steps.title: Tell Us Once notifies HM Passport Office
steps.who: Tell Us Once to HM Passport Office.
steps.trigger: Completion of Tell Us Once (the informant supplies the passport number and town of birth).

steps.title: Tell Us Once notifies DVLA
steps.who: Tell Us Once to the Driver and Vehicle Licensing Agency.
steps.summary: The driving licence is cancelled, the person removed as keeper of up to five vehicles and vehicle tax ended.

steps.title: Tell Us Once notifies the local council
steps.who: Tell Us Once to the deceased's local council.
steps.summary: The council cancels Housing Benefit, Council Tax Reduction and a Blue Badge, and informs council housing services.

steps.title: Tell Us Once removes the person from the electoral register
steps.who: Tell Us Once, through the local council, to the electoral registration officer.
steps.summary: The council is asked to remove the person from the electoral register. (Electoral registration officers in Great Britain can also inspect registrars' records directly: see the England and Wales and Scotland files.)

steps.title: Tell Us Once notifies Veterans UK, Social Security Scotland and public sector pension schemes
steps.who: Veterans UK (Armed Forces Compensation Scheme), Social Security Scotland, and public sector pension schemes (Armed Forces, Civil Service, Local Government, NHS England and Wales, Pension Protection Fund, Scottish Public Pensions Agency).
steps.summary: Tell Us Once also stops payments from these schemes; private and workplace pension schemes outside this list are not told.

steps.title: Without Tell Us Once, the family tells HMRC and others directly
steps.who: The family or personal representative, where Tell Us Once cannot be used (for example, the deceased lived in Northern Ireland or abroad).
steps.summary: HMRC is told through its Bereavement Helpline or form P1000; other bodies (Child Benefit Office, National Insurance Contributions Office, pension schemes) are contacted one by one.

steps.title: Family tells banks, insurers and other private bodies
steps.trigger: The death; usually after registration so a certificate can be shown.
steps.summary: Tell Us Once reaches only government bodies. Banks, mortgage lenders, insurers, utilities, landlords and private or workplace pension schemes must be contacted by the family; there is no official death-data feed or query service for private bodies in force.

centralPopulationRegister.note: The UK has no population register. Death is propagated by statutory feeds from registrars to DWP and by the opt-in Tell Us Once service, not by updating a central register that other bodies read from.

governmentPropagation.note: Great Britain: DWP is told automatically on registration (2012 Regulations), but HMRC, HM Passport Office, DVLA, councils and public pension schemes are told only if the family uses Tell Us Once. Not available for Northern Ireland residents (see uk-ni).

privateSectorVerification.note: No official UK-wide route for banks or insurers to check or be told of deaths; they rely on the family and a certificate. The Data (Use and Access) Act 2025 s. 45 gateway (public authorities may disclose information to registered digital verification services at an individual's request) is shown as prospective and is not death-specific. Scotland and Northern Ireland have narrow registrar-general notification powers (see those files).

gaps: HM Passport Office, DVLA and HMRC each have their own GOV.UK pages; www.hmpo.gov.uk and www.dvla.gov.uk were blocked by egress policy, so their onward handling is cited only from the Tell Us Once guide.

No statute was found that makes Tell Us Once itself mandatory or names its participating bodies; the list is from GOV.UK guidance. The legal hook found is the 'notification service' definition in SI 2012/1604 reg. 1(2).

Whether GRO's death data reaches HM Passport Office or NHS systems automatically (outside Tell Us Once) was not established from a primary source; NHS Digital / NHS England pages (www.england.nhs.uk) were blocked. England and Wales disclosure gateways (Registration Service Act 1953 s. 19AA and Statistics and Registration Service Act 2007 s. 42) are recorded in uk-ew.
The GRO Life Event Access Point (LEAP) service for public bodies was not found on a reachable official page and is not recorded.

Data (Use and Access) Act 2025 s. 45 (information gateway to registered digital verification services) is marked prospective on legislation.gov.uk as of 2026-10-28; whether GRO death data will be offered through it is unknown.

No official verification route for private bodies (an equivalent of the US LADMF) was found; commercial and industry death-notification services exist but are outside the sourcing rule and not recorded.
